title: Categories and homological methods
organizing_question: Which constructions preserve the object, and what explicit maps certify preservation?
core_objects: resolutions, Tor, Ext and cotangent complexes
filtrations, page differentials and inverse systems
overview:
This domain supplies the architecture used to compose the rest of the atlas. Its organizing unit is a construction together with the equations that make it valid. A category needs a declared class of morphisms and a composition law; a dynamical intertwiner must commute with evolution. A quotient needs an equivalence relation; its universal factorization identifies exactly which maps survive the loss of distinctions. A pushout needs two arrows from shared data and produces one object encoding all compatible pairs of outgoing maps. These examples give a precise language for composing mathematics without treating a common label or equal dimension as a structural identification.

The next layer is homological. A complex is more than a sequence of vector spaces because its differential must square to zero. Signed totalization, shifts and cones make this requirement explicit across degrees. A chain contraction gives a finite certificate that a reduction preserves cohomology. Its homotopy exhibits the difference between the identity and a reduced reconstruction as a boundary correction. This is the appropriate bridge to smaller models: one may eliminate a contractible pair while preserving homology, even though total coordinate dimension changes. The chapter therefore separates presentation size, rank information and invariant content.

Derived constructions retain information that ordinary products and kernels erase. Tor and Ext arise by resolving an object before applying a nonexact functor. A nonzero extension class can distinguish modules with identical dimension; the size of the whole Ext group cannot decide whether one selected extension splits. Similarly a tangent complex supplies potential obstruction spaces, while the actual higher-order lifting equation determines an obstruction class. The double-point and finite Maurer–Cartan examples show both outcomes: a nonzero first-order direction can fail to lift, while a nonzero quadratic cocycle can be removable because it is a boundary. These are constructive alternatives with explicit witnesses.

Finally, filtered and infinite constructions state what remains unknown after a partial computation. The associated graded forgets how layers attach. Page differentials can kill apparent classes, and integral extensions can distinguish groups with identical limiting graded pieces. Inverse limits introduce genuinely infinite compatibility constraints that finite truncations do not settle. Perverse shifts, coefficient base change and t-structures belong in this same discipline of declared data: they change the interpretation of degrees and comparisons. The dated source continuity is strongest from the 2024 categorical and spectral questions through the 2025 derived examples to the 2026 exact signs, limits and obstruction calculations. Those dates locate topics in the available corpus; they do not date the creation of the new proofs here.

The interactive capacity is consequently a certificate interface. Finite matrices can test d²=0, construct a cone, verify a contraction and compare homology. They cannot manufacture the missing differential, functor or higher coherence map of an unspecified object. The chapter’s open frontier is to replace those absent operators with explicit constructions and then verify comparison maps at the correct coefficient and categorical level.
open_frontier: Build actual comparison functors, controlling complexes and higher-coherence maps for the proposed structures; compute unknown differentials and extension classes before claiming equivalence or reconstruction.

title: Topology, cohomology and gluing
organizing_question: Which global features survive local changes, and which exact obstruction prevents a global construction?
core_objects: spaces with declared cells and attachments
overview:
The topological domain is organized around two constructive tasks: calculate an invariant of a specified space, and identify an obstruction to assembling local information globally. The first begins with cells and boundaries. A graph, the surface on which it is drawn and a filling of its cycles are different spaces. Their boundary matrices make the distinction exact. A triangle boundary has a one-dimensional cycle; attaching its face kills that class. The same principle scales to flag complexes, polyhedral boundaries and singular links, where the problem is to state the actual attachment data before assigning a homology group.

Coefficients determine what the calculation can see. Rational Betti numbers retain free rank but erase torsion. Integer normal forms supply the finite abelian groups hidden by that compression, and reduction modulo a prime can reveal a different pattern again. Reduced homology and intersection homology refine different aspects of a space: one adjusts the degree-zero basepoint contribution, while the other controls allowable chains near specified singular strata. The contractible cone on a torus makes the latter concrete, because ordinary bounding disks may be disallowed at the apex. These distinctions improve classification questions by matching the invariant to the equivalence relation and phenomenon under study.

Persistence adds maps and time to this framework. It retains finite-lived classes that disappear in the eventual space. A legal filtration orders cells after their faces, and induced maps determine births and deaths. Small exact examples support a clear interactive model, while shifted sublevel inclusions give a direct perturbation certificate. Random entry times connect topological lifetimes to order statistics in the simple square example. The scope stays explicit: a stable barcode is a controlled invariant of the declared filtration, not a complete reconstruction of the geometry or a validation of the mechanism generating the data.

The local-to-global side starts with the sheaf axiom’s actual content: compatible data glue uniquely. Arbitrary discrepancies need not be compatible, and their failure can occupy a nonzero cohomology group. Incidence equations, cycle periods and rank-one transport give complete exact examples. Discrete Hodge theory chooses harmonic representatives after an inner product is declared; it does not make every harmonic vector a zero class. Consequently a small residual or a successful test vector cannot certify disappearance of an entire obstruction space. A comparison between local models needs a cochain equivalence if it is to preserve those classes.

Periods, group multipliers and characteristic classes connect this algebraic computation to geometric invariance. Rephasing changes a multiplier by a coboundary, nonvanishing loop homotopies preserve winding, and normalized bundle curvature represents characteristic classes. The family treatments keep their degrees and coefficients separate while exposing their shared local-choice versus global-defect mechanism. This makes the domain’s interactive capacity concrete: supply a finite complex or transport system, and return a cycle, a potential, a barcode or a nonzero obstruction certificate. The frontier is to recover missing attachment, coefficient and comparison data in larger historical proposals rather than infer topology from terminology.
open_frontier: Specify the spaces, coefficient systems, legal filtrations and attachment maps in the larger proposals; produce integer certificates and valid cochain comparisons that preserve the intended global obstruction.

title: Differential and symplectic geometry
organizing_question: What becomes computable once the metric, form, connection and symmetry are explicitly declared?
core_objects: moving frames, curvature functionals and geometric curves
overview:
This domain connects local geometric structure to calculable global behavior. The first input is a declared metric, differential form or connection. Coordinates alone supply none of these. Once a metric is given, one can derive length, geodesics, curvature, volume growth and spectral scaling; once a symplectic form and Hamiltonian are given, one can derive a vector field and test conservation. This order of construction turns the archive’s geometric vocabulary into a set of mathematical interfaces with explicit assumptions and outputs.

Metric geometry separates representation changes from genuine geometric deformation. The hyperbolic half-plane has computable Christoffel symbols, vertical unit-speed geodesics and curvature minus one. Its exponential volume growth prevents a global Euclidean doubling argument even though every smooth point is locally Euclidean in the appropriate sense. Constant scaling links length, curvature and spectral thresholds through exact powers. Discrete transport curvature and prefix ultrametrics then show how different metric inputs answer different questions: probability measures matter for Ollivier curvature, while digit carries obstruct the inverse inference from real distance to prefix agreement. Neither a positive weight table nor an unexplained singular value is a metric-independent invariant.

Symplectic and contact geometry organize mechanics and reduction. Conservation of one Hamiltonian does not make it a Casimir. Removing a cyclic coordinate is a legitimate reduction only at a fixed momentum level, where the restricted two-form’s null directions are precisely the symmetry directions being quotiented. A regular moment-map quotient can be identified with a cotangent bundle in explicit charts. The oscillator demonstrates another kind of geometric change: a generating function blows up at a projection caustic while the underlying phase-space trajectory remains smooth. A Legendrian curve and a thermodynamic potential similarly require the contact form and tangent condition before their consequences follow.

Connections supply transport, curvature measures local two-dimensional noncommutation, and holonomy records a global loop. A flat circle system can have nontrivial monodromy; a curved connection on the plane can live on a trivial bundle; a Berry eigenline over the sphere can obstruct a global smooth potential. The exact shear loop makes noncommutativity and gauge conjugacy visible in finite matrices. It is the appropriate worked model for the interactive atlas, with a clear gap between this calculation and an empirical connection whose actual matrices or two-dimensional refinement are unavailable.

Curves and variational geometry complete the domain by integrating local data into shapes. Frenet frames are rotation equations tied to regularity, moving affine frames introduce explicit derivative terms, and linear curvature uniquely minimizes one declared curvature-rate functional. Endpoint positions or tangents add constraints and create a different problem. The same care with assumptions governs Willmore normalization and the distinction between immersions and embeddings. The source dates support continuity from 2023 Berry and affine questions through the 2024 geometric forms to the 2026 exact transport and reduction examples. The present proofs unify those dated topics without attributing new historical arguments. The open frontier is the construction of declared higher-dimensional metrics, transports and quotient data with quantitative verification.
open_frontier: Construct genuine two-dimensional transport refinements, verify regular quotient hypotheses and solve geometric variational problems with the full intended boundary conditions; distinguish representation singularities from failure of the underlying structure.
